newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin had "much more" than 3-4 bypasses - surgeon.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin had "much more" than 3-4 bypasses - surgeon.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin had a multiple heart bypass operation on Tuesday, far more than the three or four bypasses forecast in advance, chief surgeon Renak Akchurin told reporters.

"The number of bypasses is much more than the figure (three or four) you mentioned," he said. But he declined to give an exact figure, saying is was up to Yeltsin to decide whether to make this information public.
"I cannot answer this question because I do not have permission from the president," Akchurin told a news conference after the seven-hour operation. "It is his personal business."
"The main thing is that we revascularised the miocard (revived the cardiac muscle)," he said. "The formal number of bypasses is not in itself important."
Each bypass involves taking a vein or artery from elsewhere in the body and using it to divert blood around a blocked artery near the heart, thus improving the supply of blood.
Doctors had forecast beforehand that Yeltsin would need a triple or quadruple bypass, while cautioning that they would not know until they opened his chest.
